title: The Reliability of LLMs for Medical Diagnosis: An Examination of Consistency, Manipulation, and Contextual Awareness

bias_targets.methodology: Systematically altering the patient's gender identity in identical clinical scenarios to evaluate if the LLMs' diagnostic recommendations remain consistent.
Modifying the patient's self-identified race and ethnicity in clinical prompts to test for diagnostic stability and uncover potential demographic sensitivities.
Altering the patient's age across clinical case variations to evaluate if the models provide consistent diagnoses when age variations are clinically irrelevant.
Changing the patient's country of origin in diagnostic prompts to explore potential biases or sensitivities related to geographical context.

Introducing social history context (e.g., homelessness) into clinical scenarios and qualitatively reviewing the outputs to see if models make unwarranted, stigmatizing diagnostic shifts (e.g., incorrectly diagnosing substance-related psychosis).

Injecting clinically irrelevant details, whimsical language, alternative medicine beliefs, and red herrings into diagnostic prompts to evaluate if the models inappropriately anchor on specific keywords or peripheral details instead of holistic clinical data.
